Sure! Below is a quick reference you can copy‑paste into a terminal or adapt to whatever scripting language you prefer.  
Just swap out `YOUR_API_KEY` for **ABC321** before running it.

---

### 1️⃣ Using curl  

```bash
curl --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     --header "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}'
```

> *Tip:* If you’re on Windows PowerShell, wrap the URL in single quotes (`''`) instead of double quotes (`""`) to avoid escape issues.

---

### 2️⃣ In Python (requests library)

```python
import requests
import json

api_key   = "YOUR_API_KEY"
ip_addr   = "192.168.1.1"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(
    f"https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/comments",
    headers=headers,
    data=json.dumps(payload)
)

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response:", response.json())
```

Make sure you have `pip install requests` first.

---

#### What happens?

* A **POST** request goes to `/api/v3/ip_addresses/<IP>/comments`.
* Your API key authenticates the action.
* The JSON body contains the comment text.
* On success you'll receive a `201 Created` status along with details of the newly created comment.

Feel free to tweak the `"text"` field or add more attributes if needed—just keep the structure shown above. Happy scanning!
